stem:
Which word is the verb in this sentence?

My sister is a nurse.
hints: Not every verb shows an action. Some verbs tell what someone is.
Start by finding the nouns: which words name a person?
Set aside the words that name a person, and the word that only tells whose sister. The word left joins "my sister" to "a nurse". A joining word like this is a verb, even though it is not an action.

solution.methodName: Ask what job the word does

steps.action: "sister" and "nurse" name people, so they are nouns.
"My" only tells whose sister it is. It is not an action or a state of being.
"is" joins "my sister" to "a nurse". It tells what she is.
steps.why: A verb shows an action or a state of being. Am, is, are, was and were are state-of-being verbs. This sentence has no action word, so "is" does the verb's job.

trapNotes.My: My tells whose sister it is. It is not something anyone does or is.
trapNotes.sister: Sister names a person, so it is a noun. It is the person the sentence is about, not the verb.
trapNotes.nurse: Nurse tells what job she has, so it is easy to treat it as the action. But it names a job, so it is a noun.
